intro: Screens, passwords and battery: the words for talking about life online.
p.pantalla.consejo: The «ll» sounds like «y»: «pan-TA-ya». There are also cinema and computer screens.
p.contraseña.consejo: The ñ sounds like «ny»: «kon-tra-SE-nya». It is feminine: «la contraseña».
p.descargar.consejo: It is the opposite of «subir» a file. A phone with no battery «se ha descargado».
p.subir.consejo: It also means to go up: «subir la escalera». With photos, it means to put them online.
p.enlace.consejo: You hear «el link», but «el enlace» is the Spanish word.
p.aplicación.consejo: In conversation people say «app». It ends in «-ción», like «información».
p.batería.consejo: It has an accent on the í: «ba-te-RI-a». «Quedarse sin batería» is to have no power left.
p.cobertura.consejo: You say «no hay cobertura» when the phone has no signal.
p.enganchado.consejo: It is used with «a»: «estoy enganchada al móvil». It changes: enganchado, enganchada.
p.redes sociales.consejo: It is almost always plural: «las redes sociales». A single one is «una red social».
p.arroba.consejo: It is read «arroba»: «ana arroba correo punto es». It is feminine: «la arroba».
p.apagar.consejo: It is also said of fire: «apagar el fuego». The opposite is «encender».
b1.texto:
**Descargar** and **subir** are opposites: you download an **aplicación** and you upload a photo to **redes sociales**.

- Your **cargador** charges the **batería**. If it fails, **te quedas sin batería**.
- Without **cobertura** there is no internet. To join a network you need the **contraseña**.
- In Spain people say **el móvil**; in Latin America, **el celular**.
- If you cannot put your phone down, **estás enganchado**.

To read an email address aloud: **@** is **arroba**, the dot is **punto**, **-** is **guion** and **_** is **guion bajo**. So **ana.ruiz@correo.es** is read **ana punto ruiz arroba correo punto es**.
b2.f1.texto: Have you run out of battery again?
b2.f2.texto: I want to upload some photos to social media.
b2.f4.texto: Do you have the wifi password?
b2.f5.texto: I do not have it either.
b2.f6.texto: Then I will switch off the screen and talk to you.
b2.f7.texto: At last you have looked me in the eyes.
b4.titulo: The present perfect: what you have done today
b4.texto:
To tell what you have just done, use **haber** + participle: **he, has, ha, hemos, habéis, han** + **-ado / -ido**.

- descargar → **he descargado**
- subir → **has subido**
- quedarse → **me he quedado**

Some participles are irregular: **hecho, puesto, escrito, visto, roto**.

The participle does not change after **haber**. Words that often go with it: **ya**, **todavía no**, **hoy**, **esta semana**.
b4.e0.texto: I have downloaded the app on my phone.
b4.e1.texto: We have not uploaded the photos yet.
b4.e2.texto: My sister has written an email.
b5.titulo: The blue light of the screen
b5.f0.texto: In the dark room, a blue light trembles over the bed.
b5.f1.texto: It is the screen of a phone forgotten among the sheets.
b5.f2.texto: Each vibration sounds like a small insect inside the pillow.
b5.f3.texto: Ana opens one eye and stretches her hand towards the bedside table.
b5.f4.texto: Thirty new messages wait for her in an endless list.
b5.f5.texto: Her thumb slides without rest over the cold screen.
b5.f6.texto: The photos of other lives pass like leaves in the wind.
b5.f7.texto: Outside, in the street, a bird sings for nobody.
b5.f8.texto: Suddenly the phone switches off in her hands.
b5.f9.texto: Ana breathes deeply and at last listens to the bird's song.
b6.o0.refuerzo: It is the English «at», but in Spanish it is not read «en».
b6.o1.refuerzo: It looks like an a, but the sign has its own name.
b6.o2.refuerzo: That's it! «Ana arroba correo punto es».
b6.pregunta: How do you read @ in an email address?
b7.frase: Ya he ____ la aplicación en el móvil.
b7.o0.refuerzo: After «he» you need a participle, not the infinitive.
b7.o2.refuerzo: «Descargué» is another tense and does not go with «he».
b7.pregunta: You have just got the app. Which form is missing?
b8.frase: Estás enganchada a las redes sociales
b8.traduccion: You are hooked on social media
b9.o0.refuerzo: That's it! «No hay cobertura» means having no signal.
b9.o1.refuerzo: The charger gives power, not signal.
b9.o2.refuerzo: A link takes you to another page.
b9.pregunta: Which word do you use if the phone has no signal?
b10.frase: Mi hermana ha ____ un mensaje largo.
b10.o0.refuerzo: That form does not exist: «escribir» is irregular.
b10.o1.refuerzo: «Escribió» is simple past and does not go with «ha».
b10.pregunta: Escribir has an irregular participle. Which one?
b12.o0.refuerzo: A broken phone is something else; «enganchado» is about you.
b12.o1.refuerzo: Yes! You cannot stop using it.
b12.o2.refuerzo: It is the opposite: a hooked person always carries it.
b12.pregunta: What does «estar enganchado al móvil» mean?
p.dejas.consejo: From «dejar»: «¿Me dejas…?» is a polite way to ask to borrow. The «j» sounds like h.
p.quedado.consejo: Participle of «quedarse»: «me he quedado sin batería». The «qu» sounds like k.
p.fotos.consejo: Short for «fotografías». It is feminine even though it ends in «-o»: «la foto».
p.wifi.consejo: In Spanish it is read with a «w» like in English: «WI-fi». People say «el wifi».
p.apago.consejo: From «apagar»: «g» stays hard in «apago», but becomes «gu» in «apague».
p.mirado.consejo: Participle of «mirar»: «has mirado». It is regular: -ar becomes «-ado».
p.subido.consejo: Participle of «subir»: «hemos subido». Verbs in -ir end in «-ido».
p.correo.consejo: «Correo electrónico» is email. The «rr» is strong in the middle: «ko-RRE-o».
p.electrónico.consejo: It has an accent on the «ó». It agrees with the noun: «correo electrónico», «firma electrónica».
p.oscuras.consejo: «A oscuras» means without light: «estar a oscuras». The «sc» is two sounds: «os-KU-ras».
p.tiembla.consejo: From «temblar». The «e» changes to «ie» when stressed: «tiembla».
p.olvidado.consejo: From «olvidar». The «v» sounds like b: «ol-bi-DA-do». It agrees: «olvidada».
p.sábanas.consejo: It has an accent on the first «á»: «SA-ba-nas». It is almost always plural: «las sábanas».
p.vibración.consejo: It ends in «-ción», like «información». The «v» sounds like b.
p.mensajes.consejo: The «j» sounds like h: «men-SA-hes». The singular is «mensaje».
p.interminable.consejo: It is «in-» (not) + «terminar»: it does not end. It works for masculine and feminine.
p.pulgar.consejo: It is the finger you use to slide on the phone. The plural is «pulgares».
p.otras.consejo: From «otro»: «otro, otra, otros, otras». The «h» is not in this word.
p.vidas.consejo: Plural of «vida». The «v» sounds like b: «BI-das».
p.pasan.consejo: From «pasar»: «paso, pasas, pasa, pasamos, pasan». It has many meanings: to pass, to happen, to spend time.
p.apaga.consejo: With «se», «el móvil se apaga» means it switches off by itself. Without «se», someone switches it off.
p.canto.consejo: It comes from «cantar». A bird has a «canto», a person «canta».
p.enganchada.consejo: Feminine of «enganchado». It matches the person: «ella está enganchada».
p.usarlo.consejo: The pronoun «lo» joins the infinitive: «usar» + «lo» = «usarlo». The stress stays on «SAR».
